name: Button
description: Primary action control with an orthogonal variant (visual weight) and tone (semantic color) model, loading state, and polymorphic button/link rendering.

ariaRequirements: aria-disabled (not disabled) in link mode; anchors have no disabled attribute
focus-visible ring via --focus-ring-color; Highlight outline under forced colors
a11y.reviewedNote: 2026-06-18 — platinum pass: variant/tone API, scale(0.97) press feedback, tokenized motion, forced-colors + reduced-motion handled. AT snapshots refreshed.
a11y.axeTestExempt: Interaction atom; axe asserted on Default/Primary and per-variant a11y tests.

dense: action trigger; variant (weight) x tone (semantic) matrix, sm/md/lg, surface-aware, loading + async clickAction, polymorphic button/link

usage.description: Button triggers an action: submitting a form, confirming a choice, or starting a flow. It renders a real button, or an anchor when href is given, and carries the full variant (visual weight) by tone (semantic color) matrix.

bestPractices.description: Reserve variant=primary for the single most important action in the view; use secondary or tertiary for everything else.
Write labels that name the action, like Save changes or Send message, never OK or Click here.

Use clickAction for async work so the button shows its loading state and dedupes clicks automatically; if you need a progress readout (e.g. percent complete), render it yourself in children, the component only owns the busy/disabled state.
Pair tone=error with a confirmation step for irreversible actions.
Use surface=onDark or onBrand when the button sits on a dark or brand background instead of overriding colors.
Do not place more than one primary button in the same view; it dilutes the hierarchy.
Do not use Button for pure navigation; if it only takes the user to another page, use Link (Button with href is for action-shaped navigation like Get started).
Do not encode meaning with tone alone; the label must carry the meaning for color-blind users.
Do not use Button for an on/off state; use Switch. For multi-select within a group, use Checkbox or CheckboxGroup.

anatomy.name: Icon
anatomy.description: Leading icon reinforcing the label, for example a trash icon on Delete.

anatomy.name: Label
anatomy.description: Visible text passed as children; doubles as the accessible name when no accessibleName or tooltip is set.

anatomy.name: End icon
anatomy.description: Trailing icon rendered from the endIcon prop, for example a chevron on a menu trigger.

anatomy.name: Loading state
anatomy.description: No spinner element; while loading or clickAction is pending, the whole button pulses (opacity animation), sets aria-busy, and disables interaction. Content is unchanged, so pair with a label that still reads sensibly mid-action.

clickAction.description:
Async click handler. `onClick` still fires first if both are provided.
While the returned promise is pending, the button shows its `loading`
state, sets `aria-busy`, and disables itself (deduping repeat clicks).
Rejections are swallowed after clearing the pending state; callers own
error UX (e.g. surface a toast from within `clickAction` itself).

href.description: Destination URL. When provided, the button renders as an anchor.

surface.description: Surface the button renders on; prefer this over absolute colors on tinted bands.

disabled.description: Disables interaction and dims the control.

loading.description: Shows a loading state and blocks interaction; sets `aria-busy`.

icon.description: Leading icon: a React node, a component, or a Phosphor icon name (e.g. `"arrow-left"`).

endIcon.description: Trailing icon: a React node, a component, or a Phosphor icon name.

accessibleName.description: Accessible name; required for icon-only buttons. Maps to `aria-label`.

accessibleNameRef.description: id of an element that labels this button. Maps to `aria-labelledby`.

accessibleDescription.description: Extra context for assistive tech. Maps to `aria-describedby`.

tooltip.description: Native tooltip text; also used as an accessible-name fallback for icon-only buttons.

forbiddenUse: tertiary on dark or inverse backgrounds without explicit contrast verification
isInverse on primary over transparent or gradient parents — use surface instead
pair an icon-only button with a tooltip as the *only* accessible name
nest a Button inside another interactive control. Buttons are terminal.
use a Button for inline navigation in body copy. Use **Link**.

governance.note: Contract, spec.md and props re-read against implementation during the DSDS doc-semantics pass. Hard rules promoted to must/must-not with rationale.

content.voice: Imperative and specific. A button label names the action it performs, not the object it acts on.

terminology.rationale: Names the outcome rather than the mechanism.
Reserved for irreversible destruction; Remove implies a reversible detach.

content.notes: FI and SV labels run 20-30% longer than EN. The 24-char ceiling is measured on the longest locale, not on EN.
